note: Triennial rural district council election. Polling in Tyrone took place on Wednesday 31 May 1933. Nominations were received by Mr. John F. M'Crea, returning officer: nine Unionists and five Nationalists were returned unopposed, and two divisions had two nominations, Clogher (W. H. Boyd, Unionist, and Samuel Kirkpatrick, Ind. Unionist) and Augher (Impartial Reporter, 20 April 1933, p. 5). Augher was the only contest polled in the Clogher district, and in Clogher division Mr. Samuel Kirkpatrick withdrew, leaving Mr. W. H. Boyd (U.), the sitting member, returned unopposed (Ulster Herald, 29 April 1933, p. 4). Labels are the paper's group headings. Filed on 1933-05-31, the polling day for county council and rural district elections in Co. Tyrone that year (confirmed). Returned unopposed.
correctionNote: Renamed from 'Aughentaine' to Aghintain (19 Nov 2026, w19-tidy, the owner's decision 4 of 19 Nov 2026: a division filed under two spellings takes its official name, and each round keeps the spelling it was filed under as Constituency_Name_As_Printed): the 1911 DED map (Clogher Rural District) and the Northern Ireland DED maps of 1921-69 name the DED Aghintain; the rounds were filed as Aughentaine (1899, 1902, 1905, 1908, 1911, 1927, 1930, 1933, 1936, 1939, 1946, 1949, 1952, 1955, 1958, 1961, 1964, 1967); Aughentain (1924). This round was filed as 'Aughentaine', kept as Constituency_Name_As_Printed; the old address (aughentaine) answers with a redirect to this one.
